Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) shares slipped 1.75% to $406.03 at the 4:00 p.m. ET close on November 25, extending Tuesday's roughly 9% slide after the chipmaker registered 336,934,324 shares for possible resale. The automatic shelf filing, made after Monday's close, covers shares that OpenAI and Meta could receive through warrants tied to their GPU purchases.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with AMD.

Is AMD fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

AMD GF Value chart

OpenAI and Meta can each receive up to 160 million shares through warrants with a $0.01 exercise price, according to Wisevoter coverage of the filing. The rest covers shares linked to the World Labs and Taalas acquisitions. Vesting depends on deployments of AMD Instinct GPUs of up to 6 gigawatts and on share-price targets of up to $600. AMD receives no proceeds, and neither warrant is exercisable yet.

The filing makes the cost of AMD's marquee AI deals concrete. At Wednesday's close, 320 million warrant shares are worth about $130 billion, and they vest only as AMD wins, so success and dilution arrive together. The top $600 price hurdle sits 47.8% above the close. The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 88/100, with solid profitability, a strong balance sheet and powerful momentum. GF Value of $323.27 puts the shares at a 25.6% premium and a "modestly overvalued" label, suggesting the market already credits much of the GPU ramp. The next test is evidence of actual Instinct deployments against the 6-gigawatt milestones.

The semiconductor sector has experienced heightened volatility in 2026, with several stocks retreating significantly from their 52-week highs. These deep pullbacks reflect heightened profit-taking and valuation concerns. They have also been exacerbated by shifting investor sentiment after the US midterm elections and uncertainty surrounding artificial intelligence (AI) spending.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX), which tracks 30 major semiconductor companies, is down about 40% from its 2026 peak. It plunged 12.3% on November 5, marking its steepest single-day decline since the 2020 market crash, signaling heightened volatility in the sector. Following the selloff, billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller issued a new AI warning, insisting major opportunities could be in companies applying the technology.

While the sell-off has weighed on semiconductor manufacturers, chip designers, and equipment suppliers, it may also be creating attractive entry points for investors heading into 2027. In that view, Goldman Sachs argues that semiconductor valuations have fallen to approximately 13 times forward earnings, near a three-year low, creating more attractive entry points in the sector.

Cantor Fitzgerald analyst C.J. Muse describes the semiconductor sell-off as a mid-cycle correction, rather than the beginning of a prolonged collapse in chip demand. According to Morgan Stanley analyst Stephen Byrd, the market has essentially overestimated the impact of political opposition to data center construction. Likewise, the investment bank has listed the best semiconductor and server stocks to buy for 2027.

5 Most Oversold Semiconductor Stocks to Buy for 2027

Meanwhile, Bank of America sees a semiconductor recovery in early 2027, supported by improving valuations, corporate share buybacks, and greater clarity around US policy.

Taken together, the recent pullback presents an opportunity to identify fundamentally strong semiconductor stocks trading at more attractive valuations with sustainable revenue growth, solid balance sheets, and competitive advantages.

The slide continued through NVIDIA's November 17 earnings release. NVIDIA reported Q3 FY2027 revenue of $115.84 billion, up 103.2% year over year. detail:

CRWV
CORZ
AMD
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
CoreWeave's Default Odds Hit a Record. Core Scientific Has a Big Problem ©@Jirsak from Getty Images Pro via Canva
Key Takeaways

The cost of insuring CoreWeave's debt against default hit a record, implying a 68% chance of default within five years.

About 84% of Core Scientific's revenue in the first nine months of 2026 came from CoreWeave.

Core Scientific's total debt rose to $4.41 billion at Sept. 30, 2026, and it plans to borrow more.

New leases with AMD and a neocloud will shrink CoreWeave's share, but they won't all be built until the end of 2028.

CoreWeave (CRWV:NASDAQ) stock fell 11.8% to $42.61 on Nov. 24, 2026, in a broad AI selloff, and overnight the cost of insuring its debt against default hit a record. The swap market now puts a 68% chance on a CoreWeave default within five years, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence data. On Nov. 25, the stock fell as much as 12% again before closing nearly flat at $42.57.

That's bad news for CoreWeave's bondholders, and arguably worse news for Core Scientific (CORZ:NASDAQ), which gets most of its revenue from CoreWeave. Core Scientific's stock fell 11.08% to $10.99 on Nov. 24.

One tenant pays most of the rent

Core Scientific's latest quarterly report says CoreWeave made up about 84% of its revenue in the nine months ended Sept. 30, 2026. CoreWeave leases about 590 megawatts from Core Scientific, on contracts that Core Scientific projected would bring in $10.2 billion of revenue over 12-year terms.

Wall Street's forecast depends on that rent. Analysts expect Core Scientific's revenue to climb from $759 million this year to nearly $2 billion in 2028:

Core Scientific (CORZ): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ millions, fiscal 2023-2028 (TIKR)

Management said on its Nov. 5 call that it expects to finish leaving bitcoin mining by the end of 2026. That means Core Scientific goes into 2027 as a pure landlord. About 485 of CoreWeave's 590 megawatts were already billing at Sept. 30, so CoreWeave's rent is the base of that forecast, and most of the growth on top of it depends on the AMD leases.

It borrowed billions to build

Core Scientific's total debt nearly quadrupled in the first nine months of 2026, while its cash fell back in the third quarter:

Core Scientific (CORZ): total debt vs. cash and short-term investments, $ billions, last 8 quarters (to September 30, 2026) (TIKR)

At Sept. 30, it had $4.41 billion of debt, led by $3.3 billion of 7.75% senior secured notes due 2031, against $800 million of cash and short-term investments. On the Nov. 5 call, management put the cost of building its new AMD sites at $11 million to $12 million a megawatt, and its quarterly report says it expects to raise project-level bonds for that build within the next 12 months. If CoreWeave stopped paying rent, Core Scientific would still owe every dollar of that debt.

TIKR tracks 41 analysts on CoreWeave. How many say "Buy"?

title: Is The Client Unit Still Carrying AMD Stock?
detail:
Is The Client Unit Still Carrying AMD Stock?
Trefis Team
Thu, November 26, 2026 at 6:23 AM EST 4 min read
AMD
Trade AMD on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

If you own Advanced Micro Devices, you likely think of it as a data center stock. Yet in fiscal 2025 its Client unit grew faster. Client revenue rose 50.8% to $10.6 billion. The rest of the company grew about 28%.

The catch is what came next. In the latest quarter, client revenue grew 7% from a year earlier. Management is now planning for fewer PCs to ship across the whole market in 2027. If one shareholder sent the Client team a note this week, it would be short.

What Would AMD's Owners Tell The Client Team?

Dear Client team. You are a big part of what we own. In fiscal 2025 you brought in 30.7% of company revenue. You also grew faster than the rest of the company taken together. Now the market around you may shrink. Your company is planning for PC market unit shipments "to decline by a double-digit percentage" in 2027. It also says, "we expect to outperform the market as we deliver our Ryzen road map and grow our commercial footprint". That is the one thing we ask of you. Win share while the PC market shrinks. We want you to succeed.

AMD's Client unit grew 50.8% in fiscal 2025, and it has slowed sharply since. If this stock is a big part of your savings, a slowdown like that can leave you wishing some of your money brought in steady income while you wait. The Trefis Income Solution pays a dividend yield about 3 times the S&P 500's, from 50 companies that have paid dividends for at least 10 years in a row. See what it pays.

Why Has The Client Business Slowed?

Management gave the reason plainly: "PC sell-through slowed late in the quarter as higher memory and component costs weighed on demand." Sell-through means sales to the people who buy the PCs. Client revenue fell 4% from the quarter before.

The quarter to December looks weaker for this part of AMD. Management expects "a decline in our client and the gaming segment of greater than 20%" from the quarter before. That is a forecast, not a result. Client and Gaming segment operating income was 15% of that segment's revenue, against 21% a year ago. Operating income is profit from the business before interest and taxes.

Can The Rest Of AMD Carry A Softer PC Business?

We think it can. For the quarter to December, management expects total revenue "to grow by approximately 27%" from the quarter before, led by data center growth of "approximately 50%". Data center made up "approximately 64% of total revenue" in the latest quarter. Management expects data center to be "more than 80% of our total revenue in 2027". AMD also held more cash, $15.8 billion, than debt, $8.9 billion.

title: Cathie Wood and Philippe Laffont Are on Opposite Sides of AMD Stock. Here's Who I Think Is Right.
detail:
Cathie Wood and Philippe Laffont Are on Opposite Sides of AMD Stock. Here's Who I Think Is Right.
Daniel Sparks, The Motley Fool
Thu, November 26, 2026 at 6:13 AM EST 5 min read
AMD
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Two big-name tech investors have landed in different places on Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD). Cathie Wood's Ark Invest added almost 50,000 shares of the chipmaker on Friday, Nov. 20, when the stock dropped 13%. Philippe Laffont's Coatue Management, though, owned no AMD shares at all at the end of September, according to its newest quarterly filing.

The split follows a steep slide. AMD's record close was on Oct. 6, at $649.42. As of this writing, the stock trades near $376, off about 42% over seven weeks.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

And in the third quarter, both investors sold. Only Wood has been reported buying back in since.

Cathie Wood. Image source: Getty Images.

Laffont: out of AMD twice this year

Coatue's 13F filings (the quarterly forms big money managers use to disclose their U.S.-listed stock holdings) show a fund that has exited AMD twice in 2026. It ended 2025 with around 1.24 million AMD shares, a stake then worth $265 million, and it ended March with none.

That first exit looks badly timed now. The growth stock closed the first quarter at around $203 and almost tripled by the end of June. Even after this fall's sell-off, the stock trades well above its highest first-quarter close of about $260.

Coatue did buy back in during that climb, ending June with about 96,000 shares worth about $56 million. But that was a small stake, roughly 0.1% of the $48.6 billion in holdings the filing showed.

And by Sept. 30, the position was gone again. AMD closed the third quarter at about $612, so the second exit has aged well, with shares off about 39% since.

A 13F shows holdings, not reasons. But Coatue's filing doesn't look like a pullback from chips. As of Sept. 30, the fund had over $3 billion each in Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, Micron Technology, and Lam Research. Laffont still seems to be betting big on the artificial intelligence (AI) build-out. AMD just wasn't part of it when the quarter ended.

Wood: selling on the way up, buying on the way down

Ark has traded AMD in both directions this year. After buying shares in January and February, its funds sold AMD on dozens of days from late March to late October while the stock rose. The largest sale was on Sept. 29, around a week before the record close, when Ark sold 181,767 shares worth about $110 million.
